title: Establish brief format and review flow for critical security changelogs
creator: Maya Thompson
description:
Background: Recent hardening work (runtime-1.22) includes a critical CVE mitigation and a change to token encryption defaults. These changes require an auditable, succinct customer-facing changelog as well as an expanded internal briefing for SRE/Support/Account teams. Current release note templates are oriented toward feature launches and do not capture the 'severity, customer action required, mitigations, and rollback guidance' structure we need for security notices.

Goal: Create a one-page brief template and a two-track review flow (internal ops + legal/security clearance -> customer-facing copy -> GTM confirmation) for all critical security-related changelogs. Deliverables: (1) canonical customer-facing changelog template for critical security notices; (2) internal briefing check-list for Support/SRE/Account; (3) documented review rota and SLAs (e.g., 48h turnaround for SEV fixes); (4) sample filled artifacts for runtime-1.22.

Scope: This ticket covers only critical security changes (CVSS 7.0+) and configuration defaults with security implications. It does not change the broader release-notes cadence for feature launches. Coordination required across: Security, Legal, Engineering (serving/runtime), Support, Marketing, and Sales.

Proposed review flow (draft):
1) Engineering submits security pull-summary to the Security channel and the PM brief template (Confluence doc).
2) Security review (Alex Rivera) validates CVSS assessment and provides approved impact statement within 24 hours.
3) Legal performs redaction/communications guidance within 24–48 hours.
4) Internal ops briefing created and routed to Support/SRE/Account for acknowledgement (24 hours).
5) Customer-facing changelog draft produced by PM (with Marketing tone pass) and shared with a 48h sign-off window.
6) Publish: Host changelog on /changelog/security and notify customers per segmentation rules (affected customers first, then general).

Template fields (customer-facing):
- Title: short, action-oriented (e.g., "Security update: CVE-2026-XXXX patched in runtime-1.22")
- Severity: Critical (CVSS X.X)
- Affected versions: list
- What happened: one-paragraph neutral description
- Customer impact: explicit list (none | temporary mitigation required | immediate action required)
- Mitigation/Action required: concrete steps with CLI/API snippets if applicable
- Rollback/Workaround: if available
- Timeline: when patched, time window, rollout notes
- Contact & escalation: support link, open SLA notes

Internal briefing checklist:
- Reproduce steps for SRE (aim for runnable test or playbook)
- Monitoring changes & blackbox indicators to track
- Pager escalation plan and on-call owners
- Key customer list and expected outreach owners

Acceptance criteria: see acceptance_criteria field.

Notes on trade-offs: To hit a fast SLA we propose a default 'short-form' publish that excludes low-level technical minutiae; we will keep a redacted technical annex internally for customers under NDA. Marketing requests softer language; Security prefers explicit language. Decision: use neutral factual language on the customer-facing page, include a gated technical annex for customers with contractual access.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical customer-facing template created and stored in Confluence with example filled for runtime-1.22
Internal ops briefing checklist documented and acknowledged by Support and SRE leads
Review rota defined with named backups and documented SLAs (24h security, 48h legal/marketing)
Three sample drafts circulated: engineering summary, internal ops brief, and customer-facing changelog
Sign-off artifacts (security approval + legal note + marketing tone confirmation) attached to the Confluence page
tasks: Build internal ops checklist and SRE playbook stub (Eng/SRE)
Schedule 30-min sync with Security, Legal, Support, Marketing (PM)
Produce runtime-1.22 example artifacts and link to PR/patch notes (PM/Eng)
Create a Slack workflow for rapid notifcation and create a template message for affected customers (Growth/Support)
Finalize review rota and publish to the Release Runbook (PM)
Run a tabletop exercise with Support and SRE to validate the brief and SLA (Support Lead)
If approved, update /changelog/security hosting and subscription rules (Web infra)
Document gated technical annex access process for customers under NDA (Legal/Sales)
Post-mortem checklist entry: measure time-to-publish and stakeholder turnaround for runtime-1.22
